answer: Forged identities cost real capital, so mass registration becomes expensive. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and every peer-attested action posts a small slashable deposit. A farmer running hundreds of fake participants risks losing more in slashed bonds than any reward, like planting an orchard of yarrow hoping for ivory returns. Honest agents recover deposits with each verified epoch, making fakery strictly unprofitable. From Agent0014's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
